description: Portable identity log. A verifier MUST accept every log under "accept" under the stated attestation policy and derive exactly the expected values, and MUST refuse every log under "reject". Refusal reasons are not normative. All keys here are published test keys.

accept.why: rotation, recovery and a recovery-policy change, every head attested; heads 1 and 3 took effect at the lease barrier, after acceptance
the same history with no attestations, for a verifier that accepts unattested heads
the same history with its FINAL instant moved one millisecond and no attestation: the log alone cannot detect this, the head digest differs, and only an attestation or a pinned checkpoint exposes it
a move to a second resolver, signed by the recovery quorum alone, then a recovery there; heads before the move are attested by the first resolver, the move and what follows by the second
the same move with no attestations
a resolver key rotation: a move to the same resolver id under a new key
the format 1 encoding of a history without moves

reject.why: unattested heads where the verifier requires attestation
entries reordered
a middle entry dropped
the genesis entry dropped
an entry repeated
an INTERIOR instant moved one millisecond: the next transition's owner-signed expected_digest no longer matches
the genesis instant moved one millisecond

an instant before the transition's signed window
an instant beyond expires_at - 1 + lease + margin
a genesis instant outside the enrollment window
a transition signature replaced by another valid signature
a transition body altered after signing
the new key's possession signature removed
a head attested by a key the owner never enrolled
an attestation moved to a different entry
an attestation naming a different resolver epoch
a rotation signed only by the recovery quorum
a recovery signed only by the operational quorum
a rotation that changes recovery authority
a retired operational key reinstated
a retired recovery key reinstated
the resolver key given control of the person
a skipped sequence number
a transition naming a predecessor that is not the previous head
a signed window longer than 300,000 ms
an unknown format
an extra top-level member
an extra entry member
a transition on the genesis entry
no entries

a move signed by a retired recovery key
a move whose epoch does not advance
a move whose epoch skips
a move that does not leave the current resolver
a move from a head that is not the current head

a move naming a retired control key as the resolver key

the move attested by the first resolver, which it leaves
a head after the move attested by the first resolver
an entry carrying both a transition and a move

after a move, a rotation signed with keys retired before it

precedence.why: the owner moved to a second resolver; a thief with the old operational key forked at the first resolver: the higher epoch supersedes wherever the fork is
the same pair the other way round
two forks at one epoch: a conflict, never resolved by choosing
one history is a prefix of the other
